title: Machine Learning - Digit Recognition
description: Draw a digit (0-9) on the canvas and click "Predict" to see what the machine learning model thinks you drew!

howItWorks.title: How it works:
howItWorks.bullet1: The model is trained on scikit-learn's digits dataset (1,797 samples of 8×8 images)
howItWorks.bullet2: When you click Predict, your drawing is converted to base64
howItWorks.bullet3: Python receives the image, preprocesses it to 8×8 grayscale with adaptive thresholding
howItWorks.bullet4: A K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifier predicts the digit using 5 neighbors
howItWorks.bullet5: Distance weighting gives more importance to closer neighbors for better accuracy
howItWorks.bullet6: Active learning: If the prediction is wrong, you can correct it and retrain the model live!
howItWorks.bullet7: All processing happens in your browser using PyScript!

activeLearning.title: Active Learning with Positive & Negative Feedback
activeLearning.description: This model learns from both correct and incorrect predictions! After each prediction, you can:
activeLearning.feedbackYes: Click YES if correct → Reinforces the model's understanding of your drawing style
activeLearning.feedbackNo: Click NO if wrong → Lets you correct it and retrain with the right label
activeLearning.conclusion: The more feedback you give (positive or negative), the better it gets at recognizing your handwriting!

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.description: This example demonstrates proper separation of concerns with event-driven initialization:
architecture.component2: Python - Pure ML logic, signals ready when initialized, sends only data via callbacks
architecture.component3: DigitRecognitionController - Manages communication layer between Python and UI
architecture.component4: Svelte Components - Pure UI rendering with reactive state
